newsitem.title: CHINA: HK banks to continue to support market's record run.
newsitem.headline: HK banks to continue to support market's record run.

text.p: Hong Kong banks are forecast to continue to support the Hang Seng Index's record-breaking run with analysts differing only on whether investors maintain a market weighting or an overweight position in the sector.
"We overweight the banking sector in Hong Kong ahead of the interim results, despite its stellar performance in 1997," said regional banking analyst Peter Redhead at ING Barings.
The Hang Seng Index closed on Thursday at an all time high of 16,365.71 for a gain of 21.66 percent since the start of the year.

While this performance was built on the back of renewed enthusiasm for property stocks, the banking sector, in particular HSBC Holdings Plc which has risen 63.14 percent to HK$268.00, has led the market's rise for most of 1997.
Hang Seng Bank Ltd has risen 20.21 percent over the year to HK$113.00, while the Bank of East Asia Ltd shed 6.40 of its end 1996 value, closing on Thursday at HK$32.20.
The Bank of East Asia rose 48.76 percent in 1996, significantly outperforming the Hang Seng Index's 33.53 percent advance.

Banking stocks offer a positive alternative avenue to investment in the property sector or utilities, which have either a cloudy outlook or have had very strong earnings performances in the past three months, said Redhead.
But so have banks and this is making some analysts cautious.
"We recommend a market weight at this point," said Roland Bruce, banking analyst at NAVA SC Securties.

"Some banks' earnings could be stronger in the second half than the first half, but we still have a questions about the outlook for the prime-HIBOR (Hong Kong interbank offered rate) spread and loan growth in the second half."
Most banks have made dramatic gains in recent weeks on various fundamental and technical factors and on pure speculative rumours.
Loan growth has been so strong that some banks are estimated to have lent the equivalent of their 1996 advances in just the first six months of this year.

A key statement on the outlook for the sector came from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Hong Kong's de facto central bank on Monday, saying it saw no need to further restrict banks' lending to property-related sectors.
Mortgage lending is the single biggest earnings sector banks and with Hong Kong's historical low default rate, one of the least risky sectors.

The other big factor which should aid banks' overall outlook is the latest confirmation from the United States that inflation remained well in check and near-term interest rate hikes an unlikely possibility.

However, analysts said the mortgage war which started in the second quarter of 1996, was likely to continue. In this battle for market share, banks have cut their mortgage rates from a traditional prime plus 175 basis points to the current estimated prime plus 25 or lower, which could reduce profitability.

"Prime-Hibor spreads may come under further pressure in the second half but this will be positive for the big banks," said NAVA's Roland. "For the others good asset growth may offset the compression in spreads."
